section: Important things you should keep in mind about these benefits:

rows.Benefits Description: • Routine foot care only when you are under active treatment for a metabolic or peripheral vascular disease, such as diabetes
rows.You pay After the calendar year deductib: In-network: 5% of the Plan allowance Out-of-network: 35% of the Plan allowance and any difference between our allowance and the billed amount

rows.Benefits Description: • Diabetic shoes and shoe inserts individually designed and fitted to offload pressure points on the diabetic foot
rows.You pay After the calendar year deductib: All charges in excess of $150 (no deductible), in- and out-of- network combined

rows.Benefits Description: Not covered: • Cutting, trimming, or removal of corns, calluses, or the free edge of toenails, and similar routine treatment of conditions of the foot, except as stated above • Treatment of weak, strained or flat feet or bunions or spurs; and of any instability, imbalance or subluxation of the foot (except for surgical treatment)

• Artificial limbs and eyes • Orthopedic braces • Prosthetic sleeve or sock • Externally worn breast prostheses and surgical bras, including necessary replacements following a mastectomy • Corrective orthopedic appliances for non-dental treatment of temporomandibular joint (TMJ) pain dysfunction syndrome • Internal prosthetic devices, such as artificial joints, pacemakers, and surgically implanted breast implant following mastectomy • Bioelectric, computer programmed prosthetic devices • Implanted hearing-related devices, such as bone anchored hearing aids Notes: • For information on the professional charges for the surgery to insert an implant, see Section 5(b), Surgical procedures. • For information on the hospital and/or ambulatory surgery center benefits, see Section 5(c), Services Provided by a Hospital or Other Facility, and Ambulance Services. • We will pay only for the cost of the standard item. Coverage for specialty items is limited to the cost of the standard item. • Preauthorization is required, see Section 3, Other services that require preauthorization, for orthopedic and prosthetic devices with a retail price of $1,000
